@graph.name: Dry Eye Disease
@graph.description: Dry eye disease is a chronic condition caused by tear deficiency or rapid evaporation, leading to discomfort such as redness, itchiness, light sensitivity, and blurred vision. Treatments can alleviate symptoms and restore comfort, but there is no permanent cure.
@graph.naturalProgression: Symptoms persist chronically and may worsen without management, although therapeutic interventions often provide substantial relief.
possibleTreatment: Artificial tears or lubricating eye drops
Environmental adjustments (humidifiers, avoiding direct air flow)

@graph.name: Dry Eye Evaluation
@graph.description: Includes tear breakup time, Schirmer test, meibomian gland imaging, and ocular surface staining to assess tear production and eye surface health.

@graph.description: Academy Vision provides expert optometric services including advanced low vision care, specialized evaluations, and access to visual aids and assistive technologies.

@graph.name: Cataract
@graph.description: Cataracts are cloudy patches on the eye's lens that cause blurred or double vision, glare, halos, faded colors and difficulty with night vision; affecting over 50% of people aged 65+. Surgery replaces the clouded lens with an artificial intraocular lens (IOL). Pre- and post-operative care by optometrists supports optimal outcomes.
riskFactor: Diabetes or other systemic health conditions
@graph.naturalProgression: Without treatment, cataracts gradually worsen over time, impairing daily tasks such as driving, reading or face recognition.
possibleTreatment: Cataract surgery with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation
Pre- and post-operative co-management by ophthalmologist and optometrist
typicalTest: Pre-operative eye evaluation including lens examination and vision assessment
Instruction to use antibiotic/anti-inflammatory drops prior to surgery
Arrangements for post-operative transportation and avoiding makeup

@graph.name: Pre-operative Cataract Evaluation
@graph.description: Comprehensive diagnostic tests performed before cataract surgery including lens and retina examination, vision assessment, intraocular lens measurements, and ocular health evaluation.

@graph.name: Diabetic Retinopathy
@graph.description: Diabetic retinopathy is an eye disease caused by high blood sugar levels that damage the small blood vessels in the retina, potentially leading to swelling, fluid leakage, vision loss, and blindness.

stage.name: Non-Proliferative Retinopathy
stage.description: Early stage with microaneurysms and fluid leakage.

stage.name: Proliferative Retinopathy
stage.description: Advanced stage with abnormal vessel growth and leakage, causing vision problems.

possibleTreatment.name: Anti-VEGF injections
possibleTreatment.description: Medication to prevent formation of new blood vessels.

possibleTreatment.name: Laser surgery
possibleTreatment.description: Reduces proliferation of abnormal blood vessels.

possibleTreatment.name: Vitrectomy
possibleTreatment.description: Surgical removal of scar tissue, blood or fluid to improve retinal viewing.

@graph.name: Glaucoma
@graph.description: Glaucoma is caused by fluid build-up and increased pressure within the eye that damages the optic nerve, progressively worsening vision and potentially leading to irreversible vision loss.
riskFactor: African American, Hispanic, Asian, Native American descent
possibleTreatment: Prescription eye drops to regulate intraocular pressure
@graph.naturalProgression: Glaucoma can progress without symptoms and, if untreated, can lead to irreversible vision loss.

@graph.name: Macular Degeneration
@graph.description: An eye condition characterized by damage to the macula leading to central vision loss. Includes dry and wet types.
@graph.pathophysiology: Drusen accumulation and/or abnormal blood vessel growth under the macula damaging photoreceptors.
@graph.naturalProgression: Dry form affects 85-90%; may progress slowly to wet form, which causes rapid vision loss.
@graph.epidemiology: Approximately 11 million Americans affected; projected to reach 22 million by 2050.

possibleTreatment.name: Anti-VEGF Therapy
possibleTreatment.description: Intravitreal injections to inhibit abnormal blood vessel growth and reduce fluid leakage in wet AMD.

possibleTreatment.name: Laser Photocoagulation
possibleTreatment.description: Use of laser to seal off leaking blood vessels and prevent further vision damage.

possibleTreatment.name: AREDS Supplements
possibleTreatment.description: Special vitamins and minerals based on the AREDS formula to slow progression in intermediate AMD.

possibleTreatment.name: Low Vision Aids
possibleTreatment.description: Magnifiers, special glasses, or electronic devices to help with daily visual tasks for advanced AMD.

@graph.description: Academy Vision provides LASIK co-management, ensuring patients receive thorough pre-operative consultation and attentive post-surgery care.

@graph.name: LASIK & Refractive Surgery Co-Management
@graph.description: Co-managed LASIK is a vision-correcting procedure where an eye care provider collaborates with a LASIK surgeon: providing pre-operative evaluation, surgical guidance, and post-operative management. LASIK complications may include infection (approx. 1 in 1,500 cases), glare or halos, under- or over-correction, dry eye, temporary visual fluctuations.
@graph.howPerformed: A hinged corneal flap is created using a microkeratome or femtosecond laser, the corneal stroma is reshaped with an excimer laser, and the flap is repositioned. LASIK risks include infection, visual aberrations (glare, halos), dry eye, enhancement need.

review.reviewBody:
I had my eye exam at Academy. Dr. G was very thorough, friendly and knowledgeable.
The staff was very helpful and friendly as well. The office is modern and well stocked with a large supply of frames. Thank you for a great experience I’ll be returning for all my future optical needs.

Everyone was professional and friendly. Grateful for the in depth tools they use to check eye health (an eye scan vs the puff of air for glaucoma test). The optometrist was friendly and patient with my questions explaining everything along the way. I  also appreciated how the staff helped me pick out frames that fit my needs including taking pictures I could share with a friend for agreement on the best pair for me.
Top notch! Great doctor and staff! We felt extremely important and very well cared for.

Everyone in the office are great. A very friendly office. Very helpful. The doctor is great love him. Don't mind going to the eye doctor at all because of them. When you really need to see him they tried to fit you in right away which is great.
Very informative office, I felt comfortable the moment I walked in for my initial appt. And I was in and out in less than 30 mins. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a new eye doctor
Dr G was amazing along with the office staff

Ive been going to Academy Vision for over 20 years, I wouldn’t trust my eyes to anyone else.  Dr Ullman is caring, honest and always answers all of my questions.  His practice is so well run, everyone is so helpful and thorough.

. Dr Mark Ullman is very caring and very thorough.
The staff is caring as well. Everyone is very friendly and they make you feel comfortable. I would Def recommend him to friends and family... *****

My visit at Academy Vision was awesome the technician was so sweet and knowledgeable highly recommended I give her a 10+ and the doctor was very professional and concerned asking many important questions about my eyes issues I recommend anyone with eye problems or just a check up give them call and the staff was great it was a fun experience.
Fantastic staff and office!
From when you first walked in they were incredibly kind and personal. The Dr was so sweet and was willing to explain everything and anything! So glad my husband and I found them!

Jess at the desk is always the glue that holds it all together. She’s always kind, polite, and “on it”. The new doctor I got to see was very nice, seemed knowledgeable, and was a positive experience. I also for the first time purchased a pair of glasses from academy. The optometrist was super nice, thorough, and the price honestly was cheaper than my usually place (Costco), so I am very happy!
Excellent service and eye care!

I have been going to academy vision for about 6 years and I love it here I have yet to have a bad experience. The front staff is always so kind and helpful, The office is very clean, and the doctors are great! Dr. Marc Ullman is very personable but is also very professional and thorough when explaining things about your glasses, eye exam, etc. He’s the best ! I’ve been to other eye doctors at the office when he’s not available and they always have done a good job as well. The glasses selection is one of the best I’ve ever seen I’m super picky and have a hard time finding frames I like. And if you’re on the fence about going here I will say my favorite thing about this place is they don’t do that evil puff eye test they have a machine that takes picture scans of your eyes to check for glaucoma etc instead and it’s way better and more comfortable.

It was a pleasure being seen by Dr. Giollombardo
From the moment I walked in, the staff was friendly and efficient, making the whole process smooth and stress-free. Dr. G was professional and has great bed-side manner, I really felt like he took the time to listen and cater to what I needed, rather than sell me some generic junk You can tell he genuinely cares about his patients and their eye health. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a knowledgeable and personable optometrist!
First class operation. Great staff , friendly and happy to help. And Doctor Ullman is the BEST !!!!
I absolutely am 100% satisfied with Dr Ulman & the staff
The staff is amazing!  Very professional, helpful and friendly.   Dr. Ullman is the best. Always on top of eye care.  Would not go anywhere else@

Just had a visit March 16 I had a prob in my one eye called academy vision and they were able to get me right in ! Met with Dr giallombardo and he was great ! Knew exactly what I needed to do and put me at ease . And showed exceptional care . Prescribed an eye drop same day and I’m already treating my eye . And he will see me again in one week ! I would highly recommend this place , staff was friendly and easy to deal with . I give it ten stars  if i could . Thanks Dr G

Kind, professional staff. Bright, clean office. Impressive new technology/equipment with a great selection of glasses. Patient, knowledgeable doctor. Couldn't ask for a better experience! Highly recommend!

jsonLd.name: Dr. Marc Ullman
jsonLd.description: Dr. Marc Ullman has been a pillar of the eye care community since 1998. Originally from Toms River, he attended Binghamton University and the Pennsylvania College of Optometry. After successfully running his own practice for nearly three decades, he transitioned ownership to Dr. Lesko and Dr. Giallombardo in early 2026 but remains a vital part of the clinical team. Clinical Focus: Dr. Ullman is the practice’s primary resource for patients seeking relief from chronic dry eye, red eyes, and ocular injuries. He prides himself on: Being one of the first to offer new treatments to his patients. Managing difficult contact lens fittings and chronic ocular disease. Providing honest second opinions and surgical consultations. Dr. Ullman is known for his sensitivity to patient concerns and his commitment to the "ultimate experience in customer service". Personal Interests: In his spare time, Dr. Ullman is an accomplished card magician, performing annually for the Captains Table fundraiser at the Atlantic City Boat Show. He also helps his wife, an entertainment reporter, and enjoys life with their famous furry French Bulldog, Winston.

openGraph.og:title: Dr. Tyler Lesko, O.D. | The Local Pine Beach NJ Optometrist
openGraph.og:description: Dr. Tyler Lesko is a local eye care professional born and raised in Lacey Township, NJ. Dr. Lesko is passionate about preserving vision through advanced technology and personalized care.

jsonLd.name: Dr. Tyler Lesko
jsonLd.description: Dr. Tyler Lesko is a local eye care professional born and raised in Lacey Township, NJ. He graduated Summa Cum Laude from Georgian Court University before earning his Doctor of Optometry degree from the Pennsylvania College of Optometry (PCO), where he also graduated Summa Cum Laude. During his doctoral studies, Dr. Lesko was a powerhouse of leadership and academic excellence. He served as the President of the Student Volunteer Optometric Services to Humanity (SVOSH) and the New Jersey Student Society of Optometric Physicians. Notably, he was the 2021 National Optometry Student Bowl Champion, outperforming students from all 23 optometry schools in the nation. Clinical Specialties & Interests Dr. Lesko is passionate about preserving vision through advanced technology and personalized care. His expertise includes: Pediatrics & Myopia Management: Utilizing orthokeratology and MiSight to change the trajectory of children's lives. Specialty Contact Lenses: Providing life-changing vision for patients through complex lens fittings. Ocular Disease: Early detection and monitoring of glaucoma, macular degeneration, and cataracts. Advanced Certifications: He is certified in Light Adjustable Lens technology and Orthokeratology. Beyond the clinic, Dr. Lesko has participated in humanitarian mission trips to Panama and local vision screenings for the Special Olympics and Lions Club. At home, he enjoys spending time with his wife, son, and two cats.
